steps: Stand in mountain pose.
Inhale and raise the arms forward and up, shoulder-width apart, palms facing each other.
Stretch from the armpits to the fingertips; let the shoulder blades slide down the back.
Keep the lower ribs soft and the tailbone down so the lower back does not arch.
Hold for 30 seconds to a minute, breathing evenly; exhale and lower the arms.
armsup.works: Lengthens the sides and the spine, opens the shoulders and chest, deepens the breath; boosts mood and energy.
armsup.watch: Shoulders up at the ears, the lower back collapsing into an arch, ribs flaring forward.
armsup.easier: Arms wider than the shoulders, or bend the elbows; hands on the hips if the shoulders ache.
armsup.tip: Stand with your back to a wall: if the lower back leaves the wall when the arms go up, raise them only as far as the back stays put.
armsup.avoid: Shoulder injury — raise the arms only as far as is painless. High blood pressure or a heart condition — keep the arms up only briefly.

bigtoe.works: Stretches the hamstrings with the back fully supported.
bigtoe.watch: The other leg and hip lifting off the floor.
bigtoe.easier: A strap around the foot; bend the lower knee.

boat.works: Strengthens the abdomen and the hip flexors, balance on the sitting bones.
boat.easier: Knees bent, hands holding the back of the thighs.

bound.works: Opens the hips and groin, good for the pelvic organs.
bound.watch: Pressing the knees down with the hands.
bound.easier: Sit high on a cushion; cushions under the knees.

steps: Stand in mountain pose.
Fold the arms behind the back and hold each arm just above the elbow with the opposite hand.
Keep the forearms against the back; draw the elbows back without lifting them.
Lift the chest, keep the knees firm; hold 20–30 seconds.
Change the hold so the other arm is on top and repeat.
boundhands.works: An easier version of the reverse prayer: opens the chest, eases stiff shoulders and neck, helps with low mood.
boundhands.watch: Shoulders rounding forward, the lower back arching to compensate.
boundhands.easier: Hold the wrists or forearms instead of the elbows; feet 25 cm apart for stability.
boundhands.tip: Keep the grip firm but not tight; the stretch comes from rolling the shoulders back, not from pulling the arms.
boundhands.avoid: Angina, migraine, eye strain, low blood pressure. A slipped disc — keep the feet apart.

bridge.works: Strengthens buttocks and legs, opens the chest, gently stimulates.
bridge.watch: Knees falling apart, turning the head while up.
bridge.easier: A block under the sacrum, hips resting on it.

camel.works: Opens the chest and the front of the body, strengthens the back.
camel.watch: Hips going back and the head dropping; push the hips forward, lead with the chest.
camel.easier: Hands on the lower back; toes tucked under.
camel.avoid: Neck or lower back injury, high or low blood pressure.

cat.works: Gentle mobility of the whole spine, warms the back, links movement to breath.
cat.watch: Moving only in the lower back; let the bend travel from tailbone to head.
cat.easier: A folded blanket under the knees; sitting on a chair.
cat.avoid: Wrist pain — on fists or forearms.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, feet together or hip-width apart.
Inhale and raise the arms overhead, palms facing each other.
Exhale and bend the knees as if sitting back onto a chair; heels stay down.
Let the torso lean slightly over the thighs, but keep the head in line with the spine.
Tuck the tailbone a little so the lower back does not arch; you should still see your toes.
Hold 10 seconds to a minute; inhale, straighten the legs and lower the arms.
chair.works: Strengthens the thighs, buttocks, back and ankles, stretches the shoulders and opens the chest; builds heat and stamina.
chair.watch: Knees running past the toes, hips dropping below the knees, the lower back sagging, heels lifting.
chair.easier: Arms forward at shoulder height or hands on the thighs; or stand a foot away from a wall and let the tailbone touch it.
chair.tip: Interlace the fingers overhead and turn the palms to the ceiling for a stronger stretch of the arms and upper back.
chair.avoid: Knee or hip problems — sit only slightly. Low blood pressure, insomnia — keep it short.

chat.works: Arms, chest and core strength; prepares for arm balances.
chat.watch: Elbows flaring out, chest dropping below the shoulders.
chat.easier: Lower the knees first, then the chest.

child.works: Rests the back, gently stretches the hips and ankles, calms.
child.watch: Buttocks far from the heels and tense shoulders.
child.easier: A cushion between buttocks and heels; knees wide; forehead on the fists.
child.avoid: Knee injury; in pregnancy — knees wide apart.

cobra.works: Strengthens the back muscles, opens the chest, mobilises the spine.
cobra.watch: Pushing up with the arms only; lift with the back, the hands just help.
cobra.easier: Sphinx: forearms on the floor, elbows under the shoulders.
cobra.avoid: Pregnancy, acute lower back pain, recent abdominal surgery.

cowface.works: Opens shoulders and hips, straightens the upper back.
cowface.watch: Forcing the hands together and arching the lower back.
cowface.easier: Hold a strap between the hands; sit on a cushion.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, feet hip-width apart.
Inhale and bring the arms up overhead; interlace the fingers, index fingers pointing up, upper arms by the ears.
Press the feet into the floor and reach up through the fingertips.
Exhale and bend sideways from the waist to the right; keep the chest and hips facing forward.
Hold 15–30 seconds, breathing into the stretched side; inhale back to centre and repeat to the left.
crescent.works: Opens and lengthens the sides of the body, keeps the spine flexible, strengthens the core and freshens the breath.
crescent.watch: Collapsing into the bending side, the chest turning toward the floor, shoulders pulled up.
crescent.easier: One hand on the hip, the other arm over the head; feet a little wider than the hips.
crescent.tip: Think of lengthening, not of how far you bend: picture a line from the ankle to the fingertips getting longer.
crescent.avoid: Acute lower back or shoulder pain — bend only a little, with a hand on the hip.

croc.works: Rest on the belly, relaxes the back, slows the breath.
croc.watch: Keeping the neck twisted to one side for long — change sides.
croc.easier: Forehead on stacked hands, a cushion under the belly.
croc.avoid: Pregnancy — rest on the side instead.

steps: Stand in mountain pose and shift the weight onto the left foot.
Bend the right knee and take hold of the right ankle or the top of the foot behind you; knees together.
Raise the left arm forward to shoulder height.
Exhale, press the left foot down and tip the torso slightly forward while pressing the right foot back into the hand.
Keep the right knee directly behind you and the chest and hips facing forward.
Hold 15–30 seconds; come upright, release the leg and repeat on the other side.
dancer.works: Improves balance and concentration, opens the chest, shoulders and the fronts of the hips, strengthens the legs; good after a day of sitting.
dancer.watch: The lifted knee swinging out to the side, the standing knee locking, the lower back pinching instead of the whole spine arching.
dancer.easier: Stop once you hold the foot and stand upright; loop a strap around the foot if you can't reach; rest a hand on a wall.
dancer.tip: Lift the leg by pressing the foot into the hand, not by pulling with the arm; the arch then spreads along the whole back.
dancer.avoid: Back, shoulder, hip or knee problems; low blood pressure or dizziness — beside a wall.

steps: Stand in mountain pose and raise the arms to shoulder height.
Cross the left arm over the right at the elbows, bend the elbows and wind the forearms so the palms meet.
Bend the knees slightly and shift the weight to the left leg.
Cross the right thigh over the left above the knee and hook the right foot behind the left calf.
Keep the spine upright, hips and shoulders facing forward; gaze at a point ahead.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; unwind and repeat with the other arm and leg on top.
eagle.works: Stretches the upper back, shoulders and outer hips, strengthens the legs, knees and ankles; improves balance and concentration.
eagle.watch: Hunching the shoulders, leaning forward, gripping the floor with the toes.
eagle.easier: Toes of the top foot on the floor beside the standing foot; palms in prayer if the arms don't wrap; back lightly against a wall.
eagle.tip: Lift the wrapped elbows a little and move the hands away from the face to feel the space opening between the shoulder blades.
eagle.avoid: Knee, hip or shoulder injury; with poor balance, do the arm wrap only, standing in mountain pose.

easy.works: A steady seat for breathing and meditation; opens the hips gently.
easy.watch: Knees higher than the hips and a slumped back.
easy.easier: Sit on a cushion or folded blanket; back against a wall.
easy.avoid: Knee pain — sit on a chair with a straight back.

edog.works: Stretches calves, hamstrings and shoulders; strengthens arms; refreshes.
edog.watch: Round back and heels forced to the floor; first lengthen the spine.
edog.easier: Bend the knees, hands on a chair seat or against a wall.
edog.avoid: Wrist pain — on forearms; late pregnancy; uncontrolled high blood pressure.

steps: Step the feet wide apart, about one leg-length.
Turn the toes out about 45 degrees.
Exhale, bend the knees and lower the hips; the knees point over the toes and do not pass them.
Tilt the pelvis slightly under to lengthen the spine.
Bend the elbows at shoulder height, fingertips up, or rest the palms on the thighs.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute, then straighten the legs on an inhale.
goddess.works: Strengthens the legs, buttocks and core, opens the hips and chest; warms up and energises the whole body.
goddess.watch: Knees falling inward or past the toes, the lower back arching, the chest leaning forward.
goddess.easier: A shallower squat, palms on the thighs.
goddess.tip: Lower the hips a little more only while the knees stay right over the toes; that alignment protects the knees.
goddess.avoid: Knee or hip injury — keep the squat shallow. Shoulder pain — hands on the thighs.

steps: Stand facing a wall about an arm's length away and place the hands on it at shoulder height.
Walk the feet back, sliding the hands down, until the body forms a right angle.
Feet hip-width apart under the hips, legs straight but not locked.
Press the hands into the wall and lengthen the arms, back and neck in one line.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute, then walk forward to standing.
halflift.works: Lengthens the spine and the backs of the legs, releases tension in the shoulders and upper back, strengthens the wrists and legs; comfortable in pregnancy because it takes weight off the pelvis.
halflift.watch: Rounding the shoulders and back, the head dropping below the arms, locking the knees.
halflift.easier: Hands higher on the wall so the angle is a little more than 90 degrees; forearms on the wall if the wrists hurt.
halflift.tip: Picture the hands anchored to the wall and the hips drawing away from it — the spine gets longer between them.

steps: From triangle on the right bend the right knee and place the right fingertips on the floor or a block about 30 cm in front of the foot.
Shift the weight onto the right leg and lift the left leg until it is parallel to the floor.
Straighten the right leg and stretch the left heel back.
Raise the left arm toward the ceiling; open the chest and hips to the side.
Look ahead, or up at the hand if the neck is comfortable; hold 15–25 seconds.
Bend the right knee, lower the left leg and come up; repeat on the other side.
halfmoon.works: Strengthens the legs and buttocks, makes the spine and hips supple, improves balance and coordination; done against a wall, it eases backache and fatigue.
halfmoon.watch: Tensing the whole body, the top hip rolling forward, weight sinking into the lower hand.
halfmoon.easier: Practise with the back of the body along a wall and a block under the lower hand.
halfmoon.tip: Don't grip: lengthen from the crown of the head to the lifted heel with each breath, and the balance becomes lighter.
halfmoon.avoid: Migraine, insomnia, varicose veins, diarrhoea, fatigue. High blood pressure — look straight ahead, not up.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, left hand on the hip.
Shift the weight onto the left foot, bend the right knee and bring it up in front of you.
Hook the right big toe with the first two fingers and the thumb of the right hand.
Press the left heel down and stand tall.
Inhale and slowly straighten the right leg forward, pressing out through the heel.
Gaze at a fixed point; hold 15 seconds to a minute, release and repeat on the other side.
handtoe.works: Stretches the hamstrings, calves and hips, strengthens the standing leg; develops balance, coordination and focus.
handtoe.watch: Leaning back or rounding forward to reach the leg, the hip of the lifted leg hitching up, the standing knee bending.
handtoe.easier: Keep the lifted knee bent and hold it with both hands, or loop a strap around the foot; stand beside a wall.
handtoe.tip: Straighten the leg only as far as the torso stays upright; once steady, take the leg out to the side with the hips level.
handtoe.avoid: Hamstring, knee, hip or shoulder injury; acute sciatica.

headknee.works: Stretches one leg and the side of the back; calms.
headknee.watch: Twisting the chest away from the straight leg; turn the belly towards it.
headknee.easier: A strap around the foot, the bent knee supported by a cushion.
headknee.avoid: Knee injury of the bent leg; acute disc problems.

hero.works: Stretches the thighs and ankles; a good seat after standing on your feet.
hero.watch: Feet turned out and sharp pain in the knees — never push through.
hero.easier: A block or cushion under the buttocks, a rolled towel under the ankles.

kneeschest.works: Releases the lower back, eases gas and bloating.
kneeschest.watch: Lifting the head and straining the neck.
kneeschest.avoid: Pregnancy after the first trimester — knees wide apart.

legsup.works: Rests tired legs, calms the heart and the mind; a gentle substitute for inversions.
legsup.watch: Holding the legs up with effort; let the wall or a chair hold them.
legsup.easier: Calves on a chair seat, knees bent.
legsup.avoid: Menstruation (some traditions advise against), glaucoma, late pregnancy.

locust.works: Strengthens the whole back of the body: back, buttocks, legs.
locust.watch: Throwing the head back; the neck continues the line of the spine.
locust.easier: Lift one leg at a time, or only the chest.
locust.avoid: Pregnancy, acute back pain, after abdominal surgery.

lotus.works: A very stable meditation seat; deep hip opening.
lotus.watch: Twisting the knee to get the foot up — the opening must come from the hip.
lotus.easier: Half lotus or easy cross-legged seat on a cushion.

pasch.works: Stretches the whole back of the body, calms the nerves, aids digestion.
pasch.watch: Pulling the head to the knees with a round back; lead with the chest.
pasch.easier: A strap around the feet, knees bent, a blanket under the buttocks.
pasch.avoid: Acute disc herniation, sciatica; pregnancy — legs wide.

plank.works: Strong core, shoulders and arms; teaches the body to stay in one line.
plank.watch: Hips sagging or piked up, shoulders far behind the wrists.
plank.easier: Knees on the floor, or forearms instead of palms.
plank.avoid: Wrist or shoulder injury, pregnancy after the first trimester.

plough.works: Stretches the back and shoulders, calms the nervous system.
plough.watch: Forcing the feet to the floor and rolling onto the neck.
plough.easier: Feet on a chair seat behind the head.
plough.avoid: Neck problems, high blood pressure, glaucoma, menstruation, pregnancy.

steps: Stand in mountain pose and hold the elbows behind the back, or join the palms in reverse prayer.
Step the right foot forward about a metre; turn the back foot out about 45 degrees, both soles pressing down.
Square the hips to the front; inhale and lift the chest.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips over the right leg with a flat back; the back heel stays down.
Let the spine lengthen and the head release toward the shin; hold 15–30 seconds.
Press into the front foot, come up on an inhale and repeat on the other side.
pyramid.works: Gives an intense stretch to the hamstrings and the chest, strengthens the legs and improves balance; calms the brain and relieves stiffness in the neck, shoulders and wrists.
pyramid.watch: The back heel lifting, the front knee locking, the hips twisting, rounding the back to bring the head down.
pyramid.easier: Palms on the floor or on blocks either side of the front foot; a shorter stance.
pyramid.tip: Make the legs stable first, then fold: adjust the feet until the lower body feels rooted before going down.
pyramid.avoid: High blood pressure or a heart condition — fold only halfway with a flat back. Abdominal hernia.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, feet together.
Interlace the fingers in front of the chest and turn the palms outward.
Inhale and stretch the arms overhead, palms facing the ceiling, elbows straight.
Lift the breastbone, keep the knees firm and the tailbone down.
Hold 20–30 seconds, then change the interlock of the fingers and repeat.
raisedbound.works: Stretches the shoulders, arms, wrists and fingers, tones the back and abdomen; helps with stiff joints and low mood.
raisedbound.watch: Bent elbows, shoulders hunched, the belly pushing forward.
raisedbound.easier: Stand with the back against a wall; feet 20 cm apart if balance is unsteady.
raisedbound.tip: Change which thumb is on top each time: the unfamiliar interlock shows which side of the body is stiffer.
raisedbound.avoid: Heart conditions, migraine, low blood pressure, insomnia, diarrhoea. High blood pressure — no longer than 15 seconds.

reclbound.works: Deep relaxation with an open chest and hips; eases the belly.
reclbound.watch: Strain in the groin; the knees don't need to reach the floor.
reclbound.easier: Cushions under the knees, a bolster along the spine.
reclbound.avoid: Late pregnancy — prop the upper body high.

steps: Stand in mountain pose and roll the shoulders back.
Bring the hands behind the back, fingertips pointing down, and join the palms.
Turn the fingers in and then up, sliding the joined palms up between the shoulder blades.
Press the palms together along their whole length, elbows moving back and down.
Open the chest and armpits; hold 20–30 seconds and release slowly.
revprayer.works: Opens the chest and the front of the shoulders, makes the wrists and elbows supple; counters a rounded upper back.
revprayer.watch: The chest collapsing, the head jutting forward, forcing the wrists.
revprayer.easier: Hold the opposite elbows or forearms behind the back instead of joining the palms.
revprayer.tip: Practise the elbow hold until the shoulders and wrists are supple enough; the full prayer then comes without strain.
revprayer.avoid: Wrist or shoulder injury, migraine, low blood pressure. High blood pressure — no longer than 15 seconds.

steps: Step the feet about a metre apart; turn the right foot out 90 degrees and the left in 45 degrees.
Bend the right knee over the ankle and turn the torso to face the right knee.
Exhale and fold forward; place the left hand on the floor or a block inside the right foot.
Twist to the right and stretch the right arm toward the ceiling.
Lengthen through the crown; hold 15–30 seconds.
Lower the arm, release the twist, straighten the leg and repeat on the other side.
revsideangle.works: Stretches the legs, spine and sides; the twist massages the abdominal organs and aids digestion; strengthens the legs and builds balance.
revsideangle.watch: Twisting deeper than you can breathe, rounding the back, the front knee dropping inward.
revsideangle.easier: Lower the back knee to the floor (a lunge) and twist from there; or use a block.
revsideangle.tip: Begin from a low lunge with the back knee down; once that is comfortable, try lifting the back knee.
revsideangle.avoid: Back or spine injury, high blood pressure — do the knee-down version. Headache.

steps: Step the right foot forward about a metre; back foot turned out 45 degrees, hips squared.
Raise the arms to shoulder height.
Exhale and fold over the right leg with a flat back; place the left hand on a block or the floor inside the right foot.
Inhale and stretch the right arm to the ceiling, turning the chest toward the right leg.
Lengthen the spine through the crown; look up at the hand, ahead or down.
Hold 15–30 seconds; lower the arm, come up and repeat on the other side.
revtriangle.works: Stretches the legs and the sides of the torso, twists and refreshes the spine, tones the abdominal organs, relieves backache and improves balance.
revtriangle.watch: Bending the front knee, losing the length of the spine, the hips swinging out to the side.
revtriangle.easier: The lower hand on a block or on the shin; the top hand on the sacrum instead of up.
revtriangle.tip: If the knee feels strained, untwist a little; the length of the spine is more important than how far you turn.
revtriangle.avoid: Back or spine injury, high blood pressure, headache. Neck problems — look ahead or down.

shava.works: Deep rest for the nervous system; the body absorbs the practice.
shava.watch: Lower back arched off the floor, chin lifted, a busy mind.
shava.easier: A roll under the knees, a folded blanket under the head.
shava.avoid: Late pregnancy: lie on the left side instead.

shoulderstand.works: Calms and refreshes; reverses the pull of gravity on the legs and organs.
shoulderstand.watch: Weight on the neck — it must rest on the shoulders; never turn the head.
shoulderstand.easier: Folded blankets under the shoulders; or legs up the wall.
shoulderstand.avoid: Neck problems, high blood pressure, glaucoma, menstruation, pregnancy.

steps: Step the feet about a leg-length apart; turn the right foot out 90 degrees and the left foot in a little.
Raise the arms to shoulder height and bend the right knee until it is over the ankle.
Exhale and bend the torso to the right; place the right palm or fingertips on the floor or a block beside the right foot.
Stretch the left arm over the ear so one line runs from the outer edge of the left foot to the fingertips.
Keep the chest open to the side and turn the gaze up only if the neck is comfortable.
Hold 10–30 seconds; press into the right foot, come up on an inhale and repeat on the left.
sideangle.works: Stretches the whole side of the body, the groins and the hamstrings, strengthens the legs and knees, tones the waist, aids digestion and opens the chest.
sideangle.watch: Sinking into the bent leg, the knee falling inward, the top shoulder rolling forward, the back foot's outer edge lifting.
sideangle.easier: Rest the forearm on the front thigh instead of the hand on the floor, or use a block; practise with the back against a wall.
sideangle.tip: Reach the top arm first, then lower the bottom hand: this keeps the side long instead of collapsing toward the floor.
sideangle.avoid: High blood pressure. Neck problems or cervical spondylosis — do not turn the head up. Lower back problems — go only halfway.

staff.works: Teaches an upright spine in sitting; the base of the seated poses.
staff.watch: Sitting on the tailbone with a rounded back.
staff.easier: A folded blanket under the buttocks; knees slightly bent.
staff.avoid: Acute lower back pain — sit against a wall.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, feet hip-width apart.
Place the palms on the back of the pelvis, fingers pointing down.
Inhale and lift the chest; draw the elbows toward each other.
Exhale and arch back gently, spreading the bend along the whole spine; keep the neck long.
Hold a few breaths, then come up on an inhale, leading with the chest.
stbackbend.works: Counters hours of bending forward, opens the chest and the fronts of the hips, energises and lifts the mood.
stbackbend.watch: Throwing the head back, bending only in the lower back, knees locking.
stbackbend.easier: A small arch with the hands supporting the lower back; stand with the back near a wall.
stbackbend.tip: Think of lifting up before bending back: the longer the spine, the safer the arch.
stbackbend.avoid: Lower back or neck problems, dizziness, high blood pressure.

steps: Stand with the feet a little wider than the hips, parallel.
Interlace the fingers behind the back and press the hands down to lengthen the arms.
Inhale and open the chest, drawing the shoulder blades together.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips, letting the arms rise up behind you.
Bend the knees slightly to ease the back and legs; lift the arms only as far as is comfortable.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; come up with a flat back, pressing the hands away.
stmudra.works: Opens the shoulders and chest, stretches the upper back and legs; helps correct rounded shoulders and clears the mind.
stmudra.watch: Forcing the arms over the head, locking the knees, the neck tensing.
stmudra.easier: Hold a strap between the hands instead of interlacing; feet wider apart.
stmudra.tip: For a stronger version, do it from warrior I: fold over the bent front leg with the hands clasped behind.
stmudra.avoid: High blood pressure; neck, shoulder, back or leg injury.

supinetwist.works: Releases the lower back and hips at the end of a practice.
supinetwist.watch: The opposite shoulder lifting off the floor; let the knees go only as far as the shoulder stays down.
supinetwist.avoid: Acute lower back pain, late pregnancy.

steps: Stand with the feet together or hip-width apart, toes spread and then softly laid down.
Rock gently forward, back and side to side, then stop where the weight rests evenly on both feet.
Lift the kneecaps and front thighs without locking the knees; draw the lower belly in and up.
Let the tailbone drop down, lift the breastbone and widen the collarbones.
Arms hang by the sides, palms facing the thighs, shoulders down and back.
Crown of the head reaches up, gaze soft and level. Breathe evenly for 30 seconds to a minute.
tad.works: Teaches you to stand straight and evenly on both feet; improves posture and balance, tones the legs and buttocks and counters slouching. Every standing pose starts here.
tad.watch: Weight on the heels or on one leg, locked knees, ribs pushed forward, shoulders creeping up.
tad.easier: Feet hip-width apart. Stand with the back of the head, shoulder blades, buttocks and heels touching a wall.
tad.tip: Watch the soles of your shoes: uneven wear shows how you stand. In the pose, imagine the legs rooting down and the torso growing lighter above the waist.
tad.avoid: No restrictions. With dizziness, Parkinson's disease or a disc problem, stand facing a wall with the palms on it.

steps: Stand in mountain pose and shift the weight onto the left foot.
Bend the right leg and place the sole on the inner left thigh, calf or ankle — never on the knee joint.
Press the sole and the thigh into each other; let the right knee open to the side.
Bring the palms together at the chest.
Inhale and stretch the arms overhead, palms together; gaze at a fixed point ahead.
Hold 15–30 seconds, breathing evenly; lower the leg and repeat on the other side.
tree.works: Develops balance, concentration and calm; strengthens the legs, ankles and feet and opens the hips.
tree.watch: The foot pressing on the knee joint, the hip of the standing leg jutting out, gripping the floor with the toes, holding the breath.
tree.easier: Toes on the floor and heel on the ankle; one hand on a wall, or the shoulder blades and buttocks resting against a wall.
tree.tip: Picture the standing foot as a root going down; once you are steady, try closing the eyes for a few breaths.
tree.avoid: Dizziness or low blood pressure — practise beside a wall. Shoulder problems — palms at the chest.

steps: Step the feet about a leg-length apart; turn the right foot out 90 degrees and the left foot in a little.
Raise the arms to shoulder height, palms down.
Shift the hips to the left and extend the torso to the right over the right leg.
Exhale and lower the right hand to the shin, ankle, a block or the floor; stretch the left arm up in line with the right.
Keep both legs straight with soft knees; head, shoulders and hips in one plane.
Gaze at the top thumb if the neck allows; hold 10–30 seconds, come up on an inhale and repeat on the left.
triangle.works: Stretches the legs, hips and sides of the torso, strengthens the ankles and knees, relieves backache and neck stiffness, tones the abdominal organs and eases digestion and period discomfort.
triangle.watch: Forcing the hand to the floor at the cost of a collapsed side, the top shoulder rolling forward, locked front knee, weight resting on the lower hand.
triangle.easier: Hand on the shin or on a block outside the front foot; practise with the back against a wall to keep everything in one plane.
triangle.tip: Rest your weight on the back heel, not on the lower hand. When you start, hold the ankle and keep the top hand on the hip until you feel steady.
triangle.avoid: Dizziness, vertigo or high blood pressure — look down, not up. Heart conditions — practise against a wall with the top hand on the hip. Migraine, diarrhoea, varicose veins.

twist.works: Mobilises the spine, massages the belly, relieves stiffness in the back.
twist.watch: Twisting from the neck first and collapsing; lengthen up, then turn from the belly.
twist.easier: Sit on a cushion; a twist on a chair works too.
twist.avoid: Pregnancy — only open twists, away from the belly; acute disc problems.

updog.works: Opens the chest and the front of the body, strengthens the back and arms.
updog.watch: Shoulders shrugged, lower back pinched; spread the bend along the whole spine.
updog.easier: Do the cobra instead: hips and legs stay on the floor.
updog.avoid: Lower back injury, pregnancy, wrist pain.

steps: Stand in mountain pose, feet together or hip-width apart.
Inhale and stretch the arms overhead.
Exhale and fold forward from the hips, not from the waist, keeping the back long.
Place the palms or fingertips on the floor beside the feet, or hold the shins.
Let the head and neck hang; lift the sitting bones and stretch the backs of the legs without locking the knees.
Hold 10 seconds to a minute; bend the knees and roll up slowly on an inhale.
uttan.works: Stretches the whole back of the body, slows the heartbeat and calms the mind; refreshes after fatigue, eases stomach-ache and period pain.
uttan.watch: Rounding the back to reach the floor, hips drifting behind the heels, locked knees, coming up quickly.
uttan.easier: Bend the knees; rest the palms on the thighs with a flat back; or fold onto a table with the arms stretched across it.
uttan.tip: For a softer 'rag doll', bend the knees, hold the opposite elbows and let the upper body hang and sway gently.
uttan.avoid: Disc problems — stop with a flat back, palms on the thighs. High blood pressure, glaucoma, headache — rest the head on a support or skip. Dizziness — come up very slowly.

steps: From mountain pose step the feet wide apart, about a leg-length.
Turn the right foot out 90 degrees and the left foot in slightly; the right heel lines up with the middle of the left foot.
Inhale and raise the arms to shoulder height, palms down; hips and shoulders stay in one plane.
Exhale and bend the right knee until it is over the ankle and the thigh approaches parallel to the floor.
Keep the back leg straight, the outer edge of the back foot pressing down; turn the head and gaze over the right hand.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; straighten the leg and repeat on the left.
warrior.works: Strengthens the legs and knees, makes the hips more mobile, broadens the chest for fuller breathing, relieves stiffness in the neck and shoulders; builds stamina.
warrior.watch: The bent knee falling inward or past the ankle, the torso leaning over the front leg, the back knee sagging, shoulders lifted.
warrior.easier: Shorter stance and a smaller knee bend; hands on the hips when the arms tire. Stand with the back heel against a wall for stability.
warrior.tip: Imagine your arms pulled in opposite directions in a tug-of-war, while the torso stays exactly midway between the feet.
warrior.avoid: Heart conditions, palpitations, heartburn, diarrhoea, heavy menstrual bleeding. With a stiff neck, look straight ahead.

steps: From mountain pose step the right foot forward about a leg-length; turn the back foot out slightly, the whole sole on the floor.
Square the hips, chest and shoulders to the front.
Inhale and raise the arms overhead, palms facing each other.
Exhale and bend the front knee toward a right angle, knee over the ankle; the back leg stays straight and strong.
Lift the chest, relax the shoulders away from the ears and gaze ahead.
Hold 15 seconds to a minute; straighten the front leg, lower the arms and repeat on the other side.
warrior1.works: Strengthens the legs and back, stretches the hip flexors, arms and shoulders, expands the chest and lungs; builds stamina and confidence.
warrior1.watch: The front knee falling inward or past the ankle, the back heel lifting, the lower back over-arching, hips turned to the side.
warrior1.easier: Shorter stance, front knee only slightly bent, back foot turned out more; hands on the hips.
warrior1.tip: If the lower back feels pinched, lean the torso a little forward over the front thigh and draw the tailbone down.
warrior1.avoid: High blood pressure or a heart condition — keep the hands on the hips. Knee, hip or shoulder injury. During menstruation.

steps: Step the feet about a leg-length apart, parallel, toes forward; hands on the hips.
Inhale and lift the chest; exhale and fold forward from the hips with a flat back.
Place the palms on the floor shoulder-width apart, under the shoulders.
Lengthen the spine: crown of the head toward the floor, sitting bones up.
Bend the elbows and bring the head toward the floor between the hands; relax the neck.
Hold 30 seconds to a minute; hands back to the hips, come up with a flat back on an inhale.
wide.works: Stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs, calms the brain and nervous system, relieves fatigue and tension headaches; a gentle substitute for an inversion.
wide.watch: Feet turning out, weight shifting onto the heels, rounding the back, coming up fast.
wide.easier: Palms on blocks, or bend the knees; or walk the hands down a wall until the body forms a right angle.
wide.tip: Rest the crown of the head on a block or bolster: this turns the pose into a calming rest at the end of the standing poses.
wide.avoid: Lower back problems or high blood pressure — do the wall version. Hold no longer than a minute; low blood pressure — come up slowly.

steps: Stand with the feet about a leg-length apart, parallel, toes forward.
Exhale and fold forward with a flat back; palms on the floor under the shoulders.
Move the left hand to the centre, under the face, and press it down.
Inhale and raise the right arm to the ceiling, turning the chest to the right.
Look up at the hand, or at the floor if the neck is tight; hold 15–30 seconds.
Lower the arm and repeat to the other side; bring the feet closer and roll up slowly.
widetwist.works: Stretches the hamstrings and inner thighs while twisting the spine; tones the abdomen, releases the upper back and opens the chest.
widetwist.watch: Twisting from the neck rather than the ribs, the hips shifting sideways, the back rounding.
widetwist.easier: The bottom hand on a block; bend the knees slightly.
widetwist.tip: Breathe evenly and go a little deeper into the twist with each exhale; come up very slowly to avoid dizziness.
widetwist.avoid: High blood pressure, headache, lower back problems; skip if it makes you dizzy.
